items.stem: What does Rust's ownership system guarantee without a garbage collector?

options.text: Memory is freed exactly once when its owner goes out of scope, preventing leaks and double-frees
options.rationale: Correct: each value has a single owner and is dropped deterministically at scope end.

options.text: All data is copied on every assignment
options.rationale: Values are moved, not copied, unless the type is Copy.

options.text: Memory is never freed until the program exits
options.rationale: Values are dropped when their owner leaves scope.

options.text: A background thread collects unused memory
options.rationale: Rust has no garbage collector; cleanup is scope-based.

items.explanation: Correct: each value has a single owner and is dropped deterministically at scope end.

items.stem: Which borrowing rules does the Rust borrow checker enforce? (Select TWO)

options.text: You may have many shared (&) references OR one mutable (&mut) reference, not both at once
options.rationale: Correct: this prevents data races and aliasing bugs at compile time.

options.text: A reference must not outlive the value it points to
options.rationale: Correct: lifetimes ensure references never dangle.

options.text: Every value may have unlimited simultaneous mutable references
options.rationale: Only one mutable reference is allowed at a time.

options.text: References can freely outlive their referents
options.rationale: That would create dangling references, which the checker forbids.

items.explanation: Correct: this prevents data races and aliasing bugs at compile time.; Correct: lifetimes ensure references never dangle.

items.stem: What does the ? operator do in a function returning Result?

options.text: It returns the Ok value, or short-circuits by returning the Err from the function
options.rationale: Correct: ? unwraps on success and propagates the error on failure, converting it as needed.

options.text: It panics if the value is an error
options.rationale: That is unwrap/expect; ? propagates instead of panicking.

options.text: It ignores the error and continues
options.rationale: ? does not silently ignore errors; it returns them.

options.text: It converts a Result into a bool
options.rationale: ? extracts or propagates; it does not yield a bool.

items.explanation: Correct: ? unwraps on success and propagates the error on failure, converting it as needed.
